class_id: an E-1 field on the document path throws and fails the whole document
feature: any document of any type (price-band ad, RHP, prospectus, ...), for any IPO status or segment, whose extraction prints any E-1 field (the exchange-owned timetable/status/listing-venue set; the three that live in ipo_details are basisOfAllotmentDate, initiationOfRefundsDate, creditOfSharesDate)
symptom: The filing persister (scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts) writes E-1 fields into ipo_details via trackField, with source always DRHP (scraperSourceForDocType hard-codes it for every doc type this persister handles). The #862 guard in FieldSourcesRepository.trackFieldUpdate correctly refuses an E-1 field on the document path by THROWING — but nothing in filing-persister caught it, and by the time trackField ran, the ipo_details upsert (and the ipos upsert before it) had already executed. The uncaught throw propagated out of persistFilingExtraction, so the whole document was marked FAILED with no receipts recorded for any OTHER field it read — one exchange-owned field sank an otherwise-clean extraction.
first_seen: Reported as GitHub issue #1016, RCA confirmed from code by a Tier A reviewer 2026-09-25. Measured population on ipodhan_staging 2026-09-25 (read-only via the sanctioned tunnel): 1 real row — Runwal Enterprises Ltd. (runwal-enterprises-ltd, status OPEN), documents.id 94d54d42-d306-450b-9975-c3cc16522189, type PRICE_BAND_AD, extraction_status FAILED, uploaded_at 2026-09-24T14:46:19Z, extraction_error 'persist: E-1 field creditOfSharesDate may not be written from the document path (source=DRHP)... See #862.'
fix_prs: scraper/src/services/filing-persister.ts: E-1 fields are now filtered out of the ipo_details write candidate BEFORE the write and before trackField is called, using the SAME set (FieldSourcesRepository's exported E1_EXCHANGE_STATED_FIELDS/DOCUMENT_PATH_SOURCES, packages/shared/src/repositories/field-sources-repository.ts) the #862 guard throws on — never a hand-list. Each refusal is a structured logger.warn (field, ipoId, documentId, docType, source, reason: 'e1-document-path-refused') and a skipped_failed_check entry; the field's receipt (what the document printed) still persists, matching the treatment of an OCR value that loses precedence. The #862 guard itself is unchanged and still throws for every OTHER caller (proven by a dedicated unit test). Failing test first: scraper/tests/unit/services/filing-persister-e1-document-path-skip.test.ts, driving the REAL FieldSourcesRepository (stub db/redis) as deps.fieldSources so the real guard is what would have thrown pre-fix (verified red-then-green by temporarily disabling the filter). Six pre-existing tests that had encoded the buggy pass-through behaviour (filing-persister.test.ts's DEEPA-oracle PRICE_BAND_AD mapping test, and five in filing-persister-ocr-loses.test.ts using a REAL extractor envelope from a live SteamHouse India price-band ad) were updated to assert the corrected behaviour.
detection_check: docs/reviews/detection-checks/e1_document_path_extraction_failed.json — SPEC ONLY today (section: notCoveredByThisManifest), naming the query (documents.extraction_error ILIKE '%may not be written from the document path%') and the one pre-existing row found. Not yet promoted into scripts/audit-detection-floor.mjs's 'checks' section — owed, tracked in that entry's owner field. The fix itself is what stops new rows joining the population; this check exists to confirm that going forward and to surface the one pre-existing row for a readmission decision (not made here; no write was performed).
